Body text

A readable paragraph has enough room to breathe without losing the connection between sentences. This specimen is deliberately longer so we can judge the line length, line height, and rhythm of normal text. It should be comfortable to scan on a wide screen and remain legible on a phone.

A second paragraph makes the gap between paragraphs visible. Café, naïve, résumé, Straße, Łódź, and “curly quotation marks” exercise the bundled fonts and glyph fallbacks beyond basic English.

Font families

DM Sans: the normal body typeface. Aa Bb Cc — 0123456789.

Manrope: the heading typeface. Aa Bb Cc — 0123456789.

System sans: an available local fallback.

Medium weight (500): a label or a little emphasis.

Semibold (600): a stronger label without an oversized heading.

JetBrains Mono: abcdef 0123456789 { } < >

Spacing and rhythm

The first paragraph begins a reading sample. The following paragraph should be close enough to feel like the same thought, rather than a new section.

This second paragraph uses the tighter consecutive-paragraph gap. Compare it with the larger gap above the heading that follows.

A clear break in the article

Headings separate ideas with more space above than below. That hierarchy should remain visible on both wide and narrow screens.
